stem: A runoff EC result is entered without identifying that the sample was runoff. What is the main data-quality problem?
choices: Runoff EC does not require a sample-type label because EC is interpreted the same way for all water sources.
The main problem is missing cultivar identity rather than sample identity.
The value is still fully interpretable as long as the EC unit is present.
The sample type is missing, so the value can be mistaken for source water, prepared feed, or another measurement context and compared incorrectly.
rationale: EC meaning depends on what was measured. A runoff sample, source water, feed solution, or root-zone extract can have very different interpretation even if the numeric EC is identical. Sample identity therefore belongs in the record so later reviewers do not compare unlike measurements.
